description:
`contrib/gates/research-review.sh` Tier 1 checks 2 and 3 grep the entire gate
context file for `cites:<key>` tokens. The context embeds each dependency's
labels (but only dependency titles, never their descriptions), so an issue whose
dependencies own `cites:` labels is required to carry bracketed citations for
literature it does not use. Observed on `7a816262`: it owns no `cites:` label,
yet the check reported the union of its dependencies' three keys and failed the
gate in text that structurally cannot contain them.

A second defect compounds it: the context also embeds `run_history`, including
prior runs' stdout. A prior Tier 1 failure message contains the literal
bracketed keys (e.g. `[GGK2025]`), so a re-run of the current script can
spuriously PASS check 3 against its own prior failure output. Check 1 is
polluted the same way: any unresolvable bracketed token quoted in run history,
the gate description, or the review prompt is misattributed to the issue.

## Fix

Scope Tier 1 to the issue under review, parsing the context JSON with `jq`:

- Owned labels: extract `cites:` keys from `.issue.labels` only, never from
  dependency labels or any other context text.
- Issue text: checks 1 and 3 match against `.issue.title` + `.issue.description`
  only, never against the prompt, gate metadata, or `run_history`.
- Preserve the existing report format (`TIER1-F<n>: ...`), verdict lines, and
  the tier-2 handoff via `exec ai-review.sh`.
- Provide a test seam (e.g. `RESEARCH_REVIEW_TIER1_ONLY=1` skips tier 2, and a
  `REFS_FILE` override) so tier 1 is testable without an AI review.
- Update the script's header comment, which currently claims tier 1 "needs no
  JSON parser" — that shortcut is the root cause.

## Success criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A regression fixture reproducing the `7a816262` shape (issue owns no `cites:`
  label; dependencies own several; run_history stdout quotes bracketed keys)
  passes tier 1 with zero label findings.
- [hard] REQ-02: A fixture where the issue owns `cites:X` but its title+description lack `[X]`
  fails check 3; one where `[X]` is present and X resolves passes; one where the
  owned key does not resolve in the registry fails check 2.
- [hard] REQ-03: A fixture whose issue description cites an unresolvable `[Zzz9999]` fails
  check 1 even when that token appears nowhere else in the context.
- [hard] REQ-04: The fixtures run from a committed test script under `contrib/gates/tests/`
  exercising the real `research-review.sh`, and the script exits nonzero on any
  fixture mismatch.
- [hard] REQ-05: `jit gate evaluate 7a816262 research-review` proceeds past Tier 1 (tier 2 AI
  review runs; its verdict is its own).
title: research-review Tier 1 misattributes dependency citation labels to the issue under review
